pages.title: A – C
pages.body:
- **Abstraction:** Focusing on the important details of a problem and ignoring unnecessary ones.
- **Algorithm:** A precise, step-by-step set of instructions for solving a problem.
- **ALU:** Arithmetic Logic Unit: the part of the CPU that performs calculations and comparisons.
- **Augmented Reality (AR):** Digital content laid over a view of the real world.
- **AutoFill:** An Excel feature that continues a series or copies data when the fill handle is dragged.
- **Barcode reader:** An automatic input device that reads barcodes using light.
- **Bcc:** Blind carbon copy: email recipients hidden from other recipients.
- **Cache memory:** Small, fast memory that stores frequently used data close to the CPU.
- **Cc:** Carbon copy: email recipients who receive a copy visible to all recipients.

pages.title: C – E
pages.body:
- **Cell:** The intersection of a row and a column in a spreadsheet.
- **CIA triad:** Confidentiality, integrity and availability: the three principles of information security.
- **Constant:** A named value that does not change while a program runs.
- **Copyright:** The legal right that protects original creative works.
- **Crippleware:** Software with features disabled until the user pays.
- **Data type:** The kind of data a value is, e.g. integer, float, string, char or Boolean.
- **Decomposition:** Breaking a complex problem into smaller parts.
- **Disk caching:** Keeping recently used disk data in fast memory to speed up access.
- **E-waste:** Discarded electrical and electronic equipment.

pages.title: E – M
pages.body:
- **Ergonomics:** Designing equipment and workspaces to fit the human body.
- **File extension:** The letters after the last dot in a file name that identify the file type.
- **Formula:** A spreadsheet instruction that performs a calculation; it begins with =.
- **Freeware:** Software that is free to use but still copyrighted.
- **Gamification:** Using game elements such as points and badges in non-game activities.
- **Iteration:** Repeating a set of instructions (a loop).
- **LAN:** Local Area Network covering a building or site.
- **Linear search:** Checking each item in a list in turn until the target is found.
- **Machine learning:** AI in which computers learn patterns from data.

pages.title: M – R
pages.body:
- **MAN:** Metropolitan Area Network covering a city or town.
- **Microprocessor:** A CPU on a single chip; the basis of fourth-generation computers.
- **Mixed Reality (MR):** Digital objects that interact with the real world in real time.
- **PAN:** Personal Area Network around one person (about 10 m).
- **Patent:** Legal protection for a new invention.
- **Pico projector:** A very small, portable, battery-powered projector.
- **Piracy:** Unauthorised copying, sharing or selling of software or media.
- **Plotter:** An output device that produces large, precise drawings.
- **Robot:** A programmable machine that can sense, process information and act.

pages.title: S – V
pages.body:
- **Selection:** Choosing a path in an algorithm using a condition (IF … THEN … ELSE).
- **Sequence:** Instructions carried out one after another in order.
- **Shareware:** Software that can be tried free for a limited time.
- **Slide Master:** The top slide that controls the design of all slides in a presentation.
- **Tab stop:** A set position on the ruler to which the insertion point moves when Tab is pressed.
- **Topology:** The arrangement of devices and connections in a network.
- **Trademark:** A name, logo or symbol that identifies a company’s products.
- **Variable:** A named storage location whose value can change during a program.
- **Virtual Learning Environment:** An online platform for teaching and learning.

pages.title: V – W
pages.body:
- **Virtual Reality (VR):** A fully computer-generated 3D world experienced through a headset.
- **WAN:** Wide Area Network covering countries or continents.
